answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before joining the market, with the stake slashed when peers prove a duplicate identity. A lone operator trying to run a tundra of fake agents must fund each one, so the cost scales linearly while honest work pays once. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a zephyr building over seasons, and a haven forms only for identities with a long, checkable history — making mass forgery expensive and slow.
